decisions.decision: Use net.createConnection to watchman daemon socket instead of watchman -j subprocess
decisions.rationale: watchman -j exits after each response (not persistent); direct socket connection is persistent and the correct approach for subscriptions

decisions.decision: Get socket path via watchman get-sockname (one-shot spawn)
decisions.rationale: Most reliable cross-platform way to find the running daemon socket

next_action: Read the current state of scripts/build-dashboard.mjs, then complete the net.createConnection refactor: finish renaming watchmanClient → watchmanSocket everywhere, rewrite startWatchmanLoop, fix sendWatchmanCommand, fix shutdownWatchman, fix onWatchmanStdout JSON parsing
context_notes: The watchman -j approach fails because the subprocess exits after delivering responses — it is not a persistent streaming process. The correct approach is to call `watchman get-sockname` once (one-shot spawn, parses JSON output to get sockname field), then open a persistent net.Socket to that path. All subsequent command/response I/O goes over that socket. The existing onWatchmanStdout line-framing logic reuses cleanly — just change the data source from stdout to socket.on('data'). The JSON parsing bug (payload = line instead of JSON.parse(line)) also needs fixing or watchResponse.watch / clockResponse.clock will be undefined.
